I will keep my full 10.1 mu in the wheat-maize rotation because that matches my land, my experience, and my well irrigation. I have farmed for many years, so I will stay with the system I know can produce stable grain for my family while some household labor is away working off-farm. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put most of the fertilizer into nitrogen with enough phosphorus and some potassium, irrigate several times because wheat in my area depends on water, and manage weeds and disease with a limited number of pesticide sprays. After wheat harvest, I will plant summer maize on the same land. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because I want stronger yield, keep fertilizer at a moderate level, irrigate when the crop most needs it, and keep field work simple with rotary tillage so I can save labor and still get the crop in on time. I am making these choices to balance yield, labor, water access, and the need for reliable production from a small farm.
